01 · Executive Summary

The Answer in One Page

Reactivation is won before the lapse and at the entry point, not at the payment field. The market's strongest services treat it as an account state with its own screen and its own offer rules, and they invest most in subscribers who never chose to leave.

1

The largest reactivation audience never decided to leave.

  • Failed payments drive roughly 35 to 38% of churn in digital media; publishers historically retried failed charges 2.6 times against 13.2 for broadcasters.
  • Apple recovers 40% of billing failures in 3 days and 75% in 16 when a grace period keeps access on; Google Play's optimized recovery roughly doubles the default rate.
So what: start with payment recovery. It is mostly configuration, it reaches the most people, and the evidence for it is the strongest in this review.
2

The best return paths are state-aware, not checkout-aware.

  • Netflix, Google Play, Apple and Strava take a signed-in returner from their account state to active in three steps or fewer, with payment kept and no plan picker.
  • The Atlantic's path takes six steps including a plan choice and card entry. The card-on-file plan removes the card entry but not a single step.
  • None of the four major news publishers reviewed documents a self-serve restart. The category leader is outside publishing.
So what: make the restart page the primary lapsed experience and keep card-preselected checkout as the fallback. No publisher owns this yet.
3

Entry points and offers decide who comes back; one-click only decides how easily.

  • A 20% win-back offer lifted onsite conversion of churned readers 88% in Piano's test (0.38% to 0.71%), and Apple gates its win-back offers by tenure and time since lapse.
  • Sign-in sessions end 24 hours after the last visit, so most returners arrive signed out. Netflix and Apple carry identity in the link itself.
  • Annual subscribers rarely come back on their own: about 5% within a year, against 20% for monthly.
So what: pair the restart page with restart links that carry identity and with written offer rules. A silent one-click charge is neither the market norm nor legal; a stated price and one consent click are.

First 30 Days for the Project Team

  1. Pull the lapse-reason mixVoluntary, failed payment and trial or gift ending, for the last 12 months. It decides the order of everything below.
  2. Audit recovery settingsZuora retry rules, Stripe account updater status, and whether any pre-expiry card notice is sent.
  3. Agree the metrics treeReactivations net of 90-day re-churn as the north star, with recovery, win-back and completion as inputs (Exhibit 15).
  4. Pick the first experimentRestart page against card-preselected checkout for signed-in lapsed subscribers, with a holdout.
02 · The Reactivation Problem

A Lifecycle, Not a Checkout

Reactivation spans six moments, from a card about to expire to a reader who left a year ago. Each moment has different subscribers, different levers and different evidence, so the project should be scoped by moment rather than by screen.

03 · Starting Point

Where The Atlantic Starts

Work to date covers one corner of the problem: a subscriber who chose to leave, still has a valid card, and comes back signed in. The two largest groups, failed payments and signed-out returners, have no journey yet.

04 · Market Landscape

Six Approaches, and Who Leads

Twenty services sort into six approaches. The leaders combine three of them: a state-aware restart, payment-failure recovery and rule-gated offers. Publishers cluster in the weakest approach, which treats a returning reader as a stranger.

05 · Flow Specimens

What Good Looks Like, Annotated

Eight real screens, each marked with what to borrow and what to avoid. The strongest share three habits: they state the account fact first, they name one action, and they put the price above the button.

06 · Design Principles

Eight Principles for a Reactivation Experience

Distilled from the specimens and the capability review. Each principle notes the strength of its evidence and where The Atlantic stands, so the team can see which ones are settled and which need a test.

08 · Guardrails

Constraints the Design Must Meet

A restart is a new contract. The law and the card networks require a stated price and an affirmative consent, so the goal is one honest click, not zero clicks.

Consent and Disclosure

ROSCA, California's renewal law (July 2025), card-network rules

  • Show plan, price, renewal cadence and how to cancel before the click
  • One affirmative action; log it and keep proof (California: 3 years)
  • Cancel through the same channel used to restart
  • Treat the charge as customer-initiated, with consent for this purpose

15 USC 8403 · California ARL · Stripe CIT/MIT

Accidental Restarts

Nielsen Norman Group on one-click risk

  • Confirm immediately and offer an undo, rather than a second dialog
  • State the refund window on the confirmation screen
  • Watch refunds within 2 days as a guardrail metric

nngroup.com

Billing System Realities

Zuora and Stripe documentation

  • A restart is a new Zuora subscription; only suspended subscriptions resume
  • Undo-cancel needs cancel-at-term-end to keep the subscription alive (TK)
  • Stripe Checkout will not redisplay cards saved during subscriptions
  • Pause maps to Zuora suspend and resume

Zuora resume · Stripe redisplay

Offer Hygiene

Apple and Piano guidance

  • Wait before discounting, or readers learn to cancel for the deal
  • Never price below new-subscriber offers
  • Cap exposure, about 2 prompts per 30 days
  • Measure retention at 30, 60, 90 and 180 days, not just conversion

Apple · Piano

09 · Sizing

Sizing the Opportunity

With benchmark defaults, payment recovery outweighs both win-back and a smoother checkout. Replace each default with Atlantic data as it arrives; the model shows its formula so the team can argue with the inputs rather than the output.

10 · Recommended Approach

Where to Start, and in What Order

Keep the card-on-file backend; it is the right foundation. Change the customer-facing bet from an easier payment step to a reactivation state with entry points, and start with the subscribers who never meant to leave.

Decisions the Team Will Face

  • Should the restart page default to the previous plan at today's price, or to the previous price?
  • Should the daily gift limit hide the card-on-file option up front or refuse at submit?
  • Do restart links need a fresh sign-in, or can a signed token stand in for a session, and for how long?
  • Is pause offered to everyone at cancel, or only to readers who cite time or price?

Appendix B

Method and Sources

How This Was Built

  • Help centers and developer documentation read directly for 20 services, October 21 to 23, 2026.
  • Benchmarks from vendor research and industry bodies, graded A to C for weight.
  • Screens from public help pages, press walkthroughs and the ScreensDesign archive; no logged-in flows were observed first-hand.
  • The Atlantic's current state from the card-on-file plan, its prototype branch and the earlier reactivation prototype.

Limitations

  • Publisher help centers document reactivation least; their low scores partly reflect thin documentation.
  • Steps in Exhibit 7 are counted from documentation, not timed sessions.
  • Impact and effort in Exhibit 13 are product assessments.
  • No figure in this report is Atlantic data; Section 11 lists the internal numbers that replace them.
